analysis.title: Best Month Of The Year Meets Near-Record Shorts: UBS Warns Of A Year-End Squeeze
key_insights: UBS Seasonality Insights (Justinus Steinhorst, published Friday) says November is the best month for the S&P 500, with an average gain of 1.9% since 1950, ahead of April (1.5%) and December (1.4%). September is the only month with a clearly negative average (-0.6%).
Over the last 10 years there has been only one negative November (2021). Halloween starts the six-month 'Buy in November' stretch, which UBS calls the counterpart to 'Sell in May'.
UBS says the positive seasonal collides with an acute short squeeze risk: net exposure is very low, gross is at multi-year highs, and shorts rose sharply in October.

Goldman Prime Services shows overall gross leverage up 1.8 points to 314.1% (86th percentile 1-year) and net leverage at 73.6% (10th percentile). Fundamental long/short net leverage is 49.4% (3rd percentile), and beta-adjusted net is also in the 3rd percentile.

Goldman notes global equities were net bought for the first time in a month. De-grossing ran a third straight week, with short covers outpacing long sales 1.8 to 1. Systematic L/S funds had their worst weekly drawdown since December 2023 (-2.17%).

The Nasdaq 100 fell about 7% in October, matching its biggest monthly decline since the start of the AI cycle (Goldman). Semis fell about 8% on Friday, the 3rd largest day of underperformance in over 15 years. S&P 500 ex-AI stocks were headed for their best month since 2022.

JPMorgan's Federico Manicardi sees technicals as supportive and expects a possible tactical bounce in AI infrastructure before year-end. JPM's positioning team is seeing bottoming signals, and the SOX vs SPX drawdown rivals 2008.
Goldman's derivatives desk told clients to rent the AI rebound rather than own it.

Catalyst 1, midterms: UBS says a Blue Sweep is the base case. Six months after election day the S&P has been higher after every midterm since 1950, averaging +13.8% with a 100% hit rate across 19 midterms. One-month hit rate is 79%, with 1974 down 12% and 2018 down 8% at two months.

Goldman's Asia desk expects AI datacenter and hardware stocks to pull back in a Democratic sweep, with the Power theme outperforming. The straddle through Wednesday's close priced a 1.51% move, less than Friday's 1.82% S&P drop.

Catalyst 2, oil: November is the weakest month for commodities (-2.9% on average) and copper's best (+1.7%). UBS says Iran tail risks remain fat and suggests swapping Energy equity exposure into Metals & Mining if oil declines. Brent futures hit $118 on Friday, a six-month high, on attacks on ships in Hormuz and Saudi energy assets.

Catalysts 3 and 4: the VIX has its biggest decline of the year in November (average z-score drop of 0.39). The MOVE Index has its second weakest month, and November is the weakest month for US 10Y yields (average rolling z-score change -0.18).

UBS says the roughly 30bps retracement to about 5% in the 10Y has helped Housing and Bond Proxies, from a 5.12% high last week. It cautions that yields falling on energy disinflation are bullish for the index, while yields falling on weaker AI growth assumptions are not.
The author agrees a squeeze is likely near term but says short covering is not investor buying. Two of UBS's four catalysts (oil rising, yields falling for the wrong reason) are already wobbling.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS cites November seasonality (+1.9% average), post-midterm uncertainty clearing, and falling VIX, MOVE and yields. Hedge fund net leverage is near lows (fundamental L/S in the 3rd percentile) while gross is high, so covering could fuel a year-end chase.
tension_points.bear_case: Brent is at $118 against its seasonal weakness, and yields are falling on weaker AI growth rather than energy disinflation. A short-covering rally is not the same as investor buying.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields falling on weaker AI growth assumptions rather than energy disinflation, and oil continuing to rise after the election.

tension_points.bull_case: JPMorgan sees supportive technicals and bottoming signals in positioning, sentiment and factor moves, with the SOX vs SPX drawdown rivaling 2008.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman's derivatives desk says to rent the AI rebound rather than own it, and falling yields on weaker AI growth are not bullish.
